final_mediator_adjudications.rationale: Both critics agree on every factual element of E_33_ADC8BC66D812799F: annual publication counts 14/18/33/87, OLS slope 23.4 works/year, cutoff constraint to records deposited on or before 2024-12-31, and the explicit limitation that the trend does not establish deployment maturity, operational effectiveness, or causal mitigation effectiveness. The only difference is the forecast_relation label: Attack C5 tags the evidence as NEUTRAL_CONTEXT, while Defense C001 tags it as CHALLENGES_FORECAST. The Defense label is well-grounded on the NoP publication-activity axis because E_33 directly measures the PMT state modality (NoP) and the observed direction (increasing, 14→87) is opposite to the forecast PMT state direction (decreasing). The Attack label is also well-grounded because E_33 explicitly bounds itself as not establishing deployment maturity, operational effectiveness, or causal mitigation effectiveness, and the observed window ends at 2024 while the forecast horizon is 2025-2027. The two characterizations emphasize different aspects of the same evidence and are both supported within the surfaced boundary. C002, which quotes the explicit limitation sentence, is unambiguously supported by E_33 and both critics agree on it.

All threat-side claims are factually agreed by both critics in Round 1. E_02_066AFE8300EDCEBB (DBIR 2023) supports the median 57% increase from 1.4 to 2.2 Gbps, the 97.5th-percentile 25% increase from 99 to 124 Gbps, the DNS water-torture growth description, and the n=10,622 incident count; both critics correctly note the metric is bits-per-second volume, not NoI incident count or frequency. E_08_3453329306E149CB (CISA KEV) supports the confirmed HTTP/2 Rapid Reset DDoS exploitation record and vendor-mitigation guidance; both critics correctly bound it as an exploitation signal without asserting prevalence or severity. E_03_06E6ABC42DA3AC77 (Mandiant M-Trends 2023) supports the 48% financially-motivated statistic and the Destructive Operations definition including DDoS; E_03_F13F996D181217BA supports the post-Ukraine-invasion hacktivism increase and the claimed DDoS/defacement/hack-and-leak activity. E_04_892BBCAA3CE5CC92 (IBM X-Force 2024) supports the Israel-Hamas conflict hacktivism observations and the DDoS readiness recommendations. No claim in either set is contradicted by the surfaced evidence. The Attack's NO_DIRECTIONAL_EVIDENCE stance for the threat NoI trajectory is well-grounded because none of these records measures DDoS incident count or frequency over time, which is the specific modality (NoI) required for directional threat trajectory assessment.

Both critics agree that E_29_CD092D34A1331D02 is a static Crossref metadata record verifying the title 'Enhancing Literature Review with LLM and NLP Methods. Algorithmic Trading Case.' and DOI 10.2139/ssrn.4996945, and that it does not report a temporal publication trend. No substantive dispute exists on this claim pair; it is correctly bounded as metadata verification rather than directional evidence.
